checks.item: start_year 1554: Jesuit college of São Paulo dos Campos de Piratininga founded

checks.item: 1560: Settlement raised to a vila (Mem de Sá moves the inhabitants of Santo André da Borda do Campo to the college)
checks.found: 'In 1560 ... by order of Mem de Sá, general governor of the colony, the inhabitants of the village of Santo André da Borda do Campo were transferred to the vicinity of the college. The village of Santo André was extinguished, and the settlement was elevated to this category, with the name Vila de São Paulo de Piratininga ... in the same year, the town council ... was created.'

checks.item: 1924: Revolt and bombardment of the city (23 days in July; about a third of roughly 700,000 inhabitants fled)
checks.found: 'In 1924 the city was the stage of the São Paulo Revolt ... lasted 23 days, from 5 to 28 July ... the federal government launched an indiscriminate artillery bombardment against the city ... a third of São Paulo's 700,000 inhabitants fled the city.'
checks.detail: Year, duration and figures match the cited passage.
